_doc: Registry of every hydra automation that can APPROVE Muso credit requests without a human choosing each request. scripts/check-credit-approval-automation.sh (CI: scripts/tests/check-credit-approval-automation.bats) fails if a cron in cron-jobs.json calls one of these entrypoints without being registered here, or is enabled while its entry has approved=false. dispatch-cv-batch.sh reads approved for credit-verification-batch and forces DRY (zero writes) unless it is true. Flipping approved to true is a captain decision: set approved_by and approval_ref (who said yes, and where) in the same PR.

r5_go.gate: The r5 GO: the go-ahead a shadow path needed from the r5 review seat, after a shadow read, before it could be switched to apply.
r5_go.approval_ref: Captain ruling 2026-11-14 ~22:4xZ, verbatim: "tell it i said to do it" (Aaron retiring the r5 GO gate by name, after Fable said the captain should retire that gate by name). Standing rule, verbatim: "there should be no humans involved except the customers giving proof and their statements."
r5_go.effect: Nothing in this registry waits on an r5 GO any more. The ruling retires the gate and turns nothing on: every entry keeps its own switch (approved, apply_enabled, doc_class.shadow) and its own approved_by / approval_ref, flipped by its own reviewed PR.
r5_go.sequencing: Fable's sequencing governs what happens before any apply (firstmate r5-gate-retire-g1). (1) D1: a 20-document known-answer set (10 planted positives, 5 mismatches, 5 blanks) through the document verifier, reported per case; positives that come back unverifiable mean the verifier is broken. The free-tier model's data retention and training terms are checked before any customer contract goes through it. credit-doc-verify runs in shadow (reads and records, applies nothing) until the known-answer set passes; apply stays off by policy switch. (2) The first 100 shadow verdicts of credit-dsp-verify are each checked against their evidence; at least 99 of 100 must be correct. (3) The first apply is firstmate's call and is credit-anchored-approve only: approvals only, excluding conflict-rule failures and the 2,441 self-duplicate groups, tagged with a batch id. (4) each change is reviewed by Fable before it is merged. (5) 2026-11-15: doc_class.shadow (document_small_track) flips only after (a) credit-anchors-push has run once and (b) the 20-document known-answer set reads 20 of 20 (Fable ruling relayed by the captain; firstmate record data/verif-fixes.md D2).

credit-trust-decide.description: scripts/credit-review.py decide --mode apply (cron credit-trust-decide-15m): trust-yet-verify on the held (unverified) queue. Provisionally approves non-big rows with no validator conflict that have ONE evidence kind (all roles trusted-confirmed, a trusted footprint of >= 3 confirmed claims in each claimed role family, or Codex on server-fetched sources with verified quoted citations on >= 2 independent domains, never crowd-edited MusicBrainz/Wikipedia alone; editorial roles only on trusted catalog confirmation under pop 30), and moves the rest to user_verification_needed (Knock asks the user for proof). The fraud/PULL/HOLD/RE-VERIFY lists in policies/credit-trust-decide.json are never approved. Writes only via muso-admin-api.sh's conditional endpoint as credit-trust-decide@hydra-ops; the wrapper re-checks this entry at the write boundary and core-backend's agentApprovalGuard refuses any row with a validator conflict.

fable-decider.description: L12 executor (scripts/credit-fable-execute.py), never scheduled. Carries out Fable-ruled tray files on disk where EVERY row carries a Fable ruling id (else the whole tray is refused). TWO scopes: (1) CLOSES (action reject): unverified / user_verification_needed -> rejected, on the decider account (MUSO_ADMIN_IDENTITY=credit-decider) with X-Credit-Automation-Id fable-decider; guards on fresh Postgres facts: same status and user, not deleted, the cited reject_* still fires or a Fable R- rule with evidence, known not big (pop 1..59, not client-sourced), no live claim by the submitter on the profile, account gate allow, not watchlisted; cap 100/day (<= 400 only with a Fable cap ruling id). (2) APPROVALS (action approve; core FABLE_RULED scope, core #11010/#11011): unverified / user_verification_needed / rejected -> approved on Fable's OWN login (MUSO_ADMIN_IDENTITY=fable = agent-fable@muso.ai), admitted by core ONLY on a server-held fresh anchor record (credit_anchor_records, written by the DSP verifier's identity) on every claimed role, pinned in the approving UPDATE; executor guards: same status and user, known-small pop 1..59, account gate allow, not watchlisted; label-path approvals provisional 7 d; cap 50/day, counted separately from closes. An approve writes only while apply_enabled is true AND apply_filter is at least the floor fable_executor.registry_apply_filter holds in code (a registry edit can tighten it, never loosen it): credit-anchored-approve rows only (rule C4:anchored/v1 citing a dsp_verdicts row), never a request with no band, a conflict-rule failure or a self-duplicate group, each measured on a fresh read where unmeasured refuses; at most per_run_cap rows a run; a batch id on every audit line of the run (credit-fable-execute.py --batch-id, listed by --batch-rows); and core's updatedIds must equal the ids sent or the run stops. Both: kill file /etc/hydra/fable-decider.disabled + this registry entry re-checked before every batch and at the wrapper boundary (verify_batch on a clean env), <= 100 ids per close call / <= 50 per approve call, read back from Postgres, one audit line per row (/var/lib/hydra/credit-review/fable-decider-audit.jsonl), stops on the first surprise. Never deletes.

document_small_track.description: [key=doc-approval-doctrine] Fable R22 (2026-11-05 20:2xZ, data/verify-sla-driver-fable-d2/ruling-R22-doc-only-approval.md): the document_small_track approval class - scripts/credit_review/doc_approve.py plus the decide.py approved_refs write. A FORGERY-CHECKED (dv-4 verified) document may approve a small-track credit WITHOUT a same-run DSP anchor. T0/T1 only (popularity 1-59; UNKNOWN = big = NO); T2/T3 keep the replacement message. Under EIGHT CODED guards, never a per-item ruling: forensics (h3 PLAUSIBLE with an extracted issuer/signatory) AND an independent cross-check positive with none contradicting; same_release (xc_dsp on this track or xc_isrc by ISRC); role (not contradicted at a trusted source, and not artist/org); claimant (clean >= 30 days or a prior approval); scope document_small_track; PROVISIONAL 7 days never lowered; caps 1/request, 5/user, 10/profile, 50 users/day, fail-closed; 100% audit for 14 days with auto-freeze on a SINGLE reversal and the requester told. Order: paid first, oldest document first. Code: hydra #1684 + the R22 delta PR. Consumed by t01b's executor and by decide.py's own class check (decide.doc_class_approved). An apply run writes a document approval only through doc_class.apply_filter, the same keys and the same reader as fable-decider.apply_filter (fable_executor.approve_filter, called by decide.doc_filter_refusals): as checked in, its outcome key admits credit-anchored approvals only, so this class writes none until that key is changed by a separate decision.

NO for T2/T3 ... Order: paid first, oldest document first.' Full ruling: data/verify-sla-driver-fable-d2/ruling-R22-doc-only-approval.md. No r5 GO stands in front of this class (retired_gates.r5_go, captain 2026-11-14); that ruling armed nothing. doc_class.shadow stays true; the conditions for flipping it are recorded in retired_gates.r5_go.sequencing, and the flip is its own one-line reviewed PR. approved is not changed by either: R22's arming condition above still governs it.

credit-removal-executor.description: scripts/clickup_drain/credit_removal.py + scripts/credit_review/removal_executor.py: clears ClickUp `action:credit-removal` tickets through the TWO intents of the credit-removal model (Fable credit-removal-flow-fable-r2 §4/§7). `hide_mine` ('this is me, but hide it from my profile') writes the served-visibility hide only: no verification, no catalog delete, reversible (unhide). `not_me` ('this isn't me / I'm not on this track') files a removal claim on the core removal gate, which hides the credit at once and decides on the deterministic public-credit rule; this automation never decides a removal and never calls a catalog delete. A proof follow-up is recorded in `credit_proof_verifications` and graded by ONE tool-less Codex call (credit_trust.llm.Provider; the metered OpenRouter rung is the shared ladder every other credit judgement uses), and the graded proof is POSTed to the gate's own proof route as evidence on the EXISTING claim (once per request+proof, never re-filing the claim); until that route exists the ticket says `proof_awaiting_gate` (proof received, graded X, awaiting gate) and the internal ask for proof is not repeated. Identity comes from the verified Intercom contact through credit_review.identity_resolver, never from the ticket text. Every write is a line in /var/lib/hydra/credit-removal/ledger.jsonl with an inverse (unhide / withdraw) and is replayable with `--revert <run_id>`.
credit-removal-executor.status_note: SHIPS UNAPPROVED, on purpose. Three separate gates must open before a credit is hidden or a claim is filed: (1) THIS entry must be flipped to approved:true with the captain's approved_by + approval_ref, because a hide is customer-visible on a named person's profile and the first batch is signed off from the dry run (one line per ticket: intent, track, roles, identity match and the disposition); (2) /etc/hydra/credit-removal-executor.live must exist, because the core routes it calls are new (C1's hide primitive, C2's gate request) and a human has to record that core really admits this automation; and (3) the routes must actually answer: while C1/C2 are unmerged every row is `authority_unavailable` (the run reports it and writes nothing) rather than falling back to the legacy removal path. Kill switches: /etc/hydra/clickup-drain-credit-removal.disabled (the drainer), /etc/hydra/credit-removal-executor.disabled (the executor), the cron's enabled:false, and this flag. Caps: 20 rows/run, 3 rows/ticket. The two intents are the ONLY actions; the cron ships dry-run.

verification-scale-drain.description: The verification scale drain (scripts/credit_review/scale_drain.py): a deterministic SQL ladder over the 92,861-request verification backlog, no model in the hot path. Approves ONLY on a row-specific evidence anchor - a per-claimant precedent match (the same claimant's earlier approved request for the same track and role set) or a proof verdict (the proof id, newest verdict wins including a soft one) - records an asked-and-expired request, or a refuse precedent that no evidence on file postdates, as cannot_confirm (a ledger row only: no API write, no message, and the row is decided again on the next plan; evidence newer than the refusal takes the request out of the precedent rule), and emits a refuse proof verdict as ask. A row with no anchor is unmatched: never written and never asked. Writes through the reviewed wrapper (PUT /admin/credit-requests) under its own requester identity scale-drain@hydra-ops, admitted by is_scale_drain_approval in muso-admin-api.sh, which re-checks this registry entry, the kill file /etc/hydra/scale-drain.disabled, the body shape (<=50 unique UUIDs) and the drain-signal digest naming an auto-approvable rule. Never sets CV_APPROVE_GATE_DISABLED. Writes no status but approved: it never writes rejected, not for a duplicate either. Never lowers a served number, never deletes, never removes a credit.

proof-review-coded.description: scripts/ops_intake/proof_review.py review --mode apply: answers a 'review the proof' ask from H3 + doc-verify + dsp-verify + the fraud lens. It APPROVES NOTHING and sends nothing itself: the only customer action it can name is one of the single sender's ask campaigns (gap-ask / uvn-status via credit-review.py uvn-status --from-stage2), and a SUFFICIENT verdict only records the ask as waiting_route. Registered here anyway so a future cron that runs it can never slip past this guard.
proof-review-coded.status_note: Cannot approve by construction: no approval writer exists (policies/proof-review-route.json approval_route.mode is off), so a sufficient proof review waits for a captain decision. Turning that on is a captain decision and a reviewed PR that also sets approved/approved_by/approval_ref here.

empty-track-approve.description: scripts/credit_review/empty_track_approve.py (ET1:empty_track_approve/v1): the captain's empty-track case (2026-11-16 02:1xZ, 'if no credits are on a track we let those go on if it makes sense?') - approve a held credit request sitting on a catalog track that carries ZERO credits, provided the track has a real ISRC or Spotify id, the claim has no role conflict (no reject_* rule, no review_* hold at 30+, no one-person-role contradiction, no organization role), there is no watchlist hit and no R8 account hold, and the account gate is a green allow. Never a track that already has ANY credit. A separate predicate from the validator low-risk path (score_approve thresholds untouched); deterministic, no model; every unreadable input is a hold. Registered here even though it ships UNAPPROVED and shadow-only, so a cron or loop that ever runs it cannot slip past this guard.
empty-track-approve.status_note: Cannot approve by construction: this module wires NO approve writer (empty_track_approve.NO_WRITER), so apply_refusal refuses even with the policy switch on and approved_by/approval_ref set. policies/credit-empty-track-approve.json ships apply_enabled:false with both fields null. Arming it is a separate reviewed change - a writer plus a Fable ruling on the copy and the arming - and that PR sets approved:true with approved_by/approval_ref here. Kill switch: /etc/hydra/empty-track-approve.disabled. It records in its own ledger table empty_track_decisions, never in the decider's decisions.
